This file lives under 03_ASSETS/Steinerne_Bruecke/ (the project's asset-registry root, same convention as 2_5D_ASSET_MAP.json) and is fetched at runtime by 04_PREVIEWS/PROTOTYPES/ZEITSPRUNG_V2/STEINERNE_BRUECKE/js/museum25d.js. Do not fork/duplicate this file into the web-slot copy folder — the web module reads this path directly over HTTP.
slot_base_note: Every slot's file_path is relative to slot_base — identical resolution rule the module previously used for its hardcoded SLOT_BASE constant. slot_base itself points at the curated WEB COPIES, never at 03_ASSETS/Steinerne_Bruecke/IMAGES/MASTER/.

video_transition_contract.$note: PHASE 2.3 — ONE-SHOT DIRECTIONAL TRANSITION CLIPS (distinct from the ambient video_loop contract above). A 'video_transition' slot is one HALF of an assembly/disassembly pair for a chapter that already has an approved still fallback image. SCHEMA CHOICE: option (b) from the Phase 2.3 brief — two sibling slots per chapter (one per pair_role), linked via a shared chapter_key + a `transition_pair` block, mirroring the pre-existing loop_pair convention used by explosion_loop/reassembly_loop. Chosen over option (a) (one slot, two file_path fields) because resolveSlot()/the loop-slot discovery pattern already resolves ONE slot_id -> ONE status/file_path uniformly; two sibling slots reuse that resolver completely unmodified, whereas a dual-file_path slot would have needed a second resolution branch inside resolveSlot() for this one type.
video_transition_contract.discovery: museum25d.js scans manifest.slots for type === 'video_transition' AND a non-empty chapter_key, grouping by chapter_key into { assembly, disassembly } pairs (via each slot's pair_role). A chapter is only offered transition playback when AT LEAST ONE of its two pair_role slots resolves (status READY + file_path). A pair_role that fails to resolve simply is not available for that direction — never a broken <video>.
video_transition_contract.render_target: 'flat_layer' = both clips are injected as
video_transition_contract.playback: NOT looping, NOT ambient. autoplay is entirely event-driven: a clip plays ONCE, exactly when its chapter becomes the ACTIVE chapter via the master timeline's chapter-change event AND the scroll direction at that moment selects that clip's pair_role (forward navigation entering the chapter for the first time in a given direction plays assembly if the chapter is being entered while the structure is becoming whole, disassembly if it is being entered while the structure is separating — see museum25d.js's TRANSITION_DIRECTION_RULE for the exact per-chapter mapping). On 'ended' (or immediately, if the slot does not resolve), the video is hidden and the chapter's existing approved static fallback image (`fallback_slot_id`) is revealed/stays visible underneath — byte-identical to today's rendering once settled. There is deliberately NO scroll-scrubbed video playback, exactly like the video_loop contract above: a transition clip plays once at its own rate or not at all, it is never scrubbed by scroll position. Only ONE video element (across BOTH the video_loop and video_transition systems) may be in an actively-playing state system-wide.
video_transition_contract.single_flight: Each chapter_key tracks its own monotonically increasing requestId. Triggering a (re)play bumps the id; the clip's own 'ended'/'pause' handlers and the play() promise resolution compare their captured id against the current one and no-op if superseded — so a stale handler from an aborted/overtaken request can never hide the wrong element or restart playback out of order. Repeated dot-nav clicks or fast scroll therefore only ever result in the LATEST requested direction's clip playing.
video_transition_contract.fallback_slot_id: Same meaning as the video_loop contract: the approved still slot this transition pair settles on / falls back to when PENDING or after the clip ends.
video_transition_contract.freigabe: Each slot's own status/file_path is the sole source of truth for whether a real approved file exists. This contract block documents mechanism only and asserts nothing about which slots are currently READY — see each slot's own entry.

display_fit_note: OPTIONAL per-slot display-fit metadata (orientation, preferred_fit, max_width, max_height, align_x, align_y, background_mode) — added to fix the 2.5D museum stage sizing so each slot is presented according to its own real aspect ratio/type instead of one fixed box. All fields are optional; a slot that omits them inherits sensible CSS defaults for its preferred_fit (or, if preferred_fit itself is omitted, a default inferred from orientation in museum25d.js). See ASSET_SWAP_SYSTEM.md section 3a for the full definitions of each preferred_fit value and how museum25d.js/style.css consume these fields generically (never branched on slot_id).

loop_slot_contract.$note: PHASE 2.2 — OPTIONAL CINEMATIC LOOP SLOTS. Every slot with type 'video_loop' is an OPTIONAL enhancement of one chapter that already has an approved still image. The contract museum25d.js implements generically (no slot_id is hardcoded anywhere in the code):
loop_slot_contract.discovery: museum25d.js scans manifest.slots for type === 'video_loop' AND a non-empty chapter_key. It builds a chapterKey -> loopSlot map at runtime. Adding a loop slot for any future chapter therefore needs a manifest entry only, never a code change.
loop_slot_contract.activation: A loop is used for its chapter ONLY when resolveSlot() succeeds, i.e. status === 'READY' AND file_path !== null. Any other state (PENDING, DISABLED, missing, null path) resolves to ok:false and the chapter falls back to its normal still-image layer, byte-identically to how it renders with no loop slot present at all. A <video> element is not even created in that case, so a broken/empty video tag is structurally impossible.
loop_slot_contract.render_target: 'flat_layer' = a <video class="museum__flat-img museum__loop-video"> is injected into #museumFlat and becomes that chapter's animated layer, inheriting the same generic display-fit system as the images. 'pending_layer' = the pre-existing #museumPendingVideo element is used instead (bau_loop_01's already-proven Phase 1/2 path, preserved unchanged).
loop_slot_contract.playback: muted + loop + playsinline + no controls + preload='none'. src is only assigned inside the module's deferred asset gate, and playback only starts while BOTH (a) the museum section is intersecting the viewport and (b) the loop's own chapter is the current chapter per the master timeline's progress->chapter map. Pausing happens on either condition failing. There is deliberately NO scroll-scrubbed video playback — the loop runs at its own rate or not at all.
loop_slot_contract.fallback_slot_id: Documentation of which approved still slot the loop would take over from. Read by nothing at runtime; the actual fallback is structural (see 'activation').
loop_slot_contract.freigabe: No video file for ANY of these slots exists on disk. reserved_file_path records the intended location only. Nothing here asserts that an approved loop exists.

slots.label: Bridge structure — single rigid depth layer
slots.notes: 1536x512 RGBA. Geometrically-locked layer — reframed only (scale/rotate/translate), never split or warped. Shared across the overview, struktur and reset sections via the same slot_id (not duplicated as three separate slots). The only true RGBA cutout among the current slots and the only landscape asset — presented free-floating (background_mode:none, no card/frame) and large (cutout_stage), scaled up via max-height rather than boxed to a small letterboxed strip. PHASE 1B CENTERING AUDIT (prior task): verified via raw alpha-bbox decode that the visible bridge content sits at ~52.1% of the 512px canvas height (i.e. ~2% below true vertical center — negligible) and, combined with the CHAPTERS overview/complete framing values ({scale:1, rotate:0, y:0}) and the flex-centered #museumPrimary layout, the layer IS already geometrically centered — no positional/offset bug found. The real driver of the reported 'excessive empty space above/below' is this asset's extreme 3:1 landscape aspect ratio (content itself ~7:1) rendered inside a tall portrait mobile stage, which is unavoidable without cropping/distorting the geometrically-locked layer (forbidden). align_y left at 'center' — confirmed via code inspection that align_y has no effect on this specific layer anyway (#museumBridgeImg's parent #museumPrimaryInner is display:inline-block, not a flex container, so CSS align-self is inert here; it only matters for the flat-layer chapters where images are flex children). PHASE 1C RE-AUDIT (this task, 2026-08-29): independently re-decoded the raw alpha channel (PIL-based per-pixel scan, alpha threshold tested at 25/32/40 — result stable across all three) and got bbox_w=95.77% / bbox_h=40.82% of the 1536x512 canvas, horizontal offset from canvas center=-1.0%, vertical offset=+2.05% (matches the prior 52.1%-of-height finding) — confirms centering is correct as-is, no numeric align offset needed (the generic 3-way align_y enum stays sufficient for this asset; the numeric-offset extension point discussed for this task was evaluated and NOT implemented anywhere in the 7 audited slots because every measured bbox offset came back under 3% of canvas — visually negligible). On max-width: because the aspect ratio is fixed at 3:1 and mobile viewports are far narrower than tall (max-height 88vh is never the binding constraint at any tested width — confirmed by computing rendered size at 375/390/393/430px: image is always sized by max-width, landing at roughly 121-141px tall vs. 88vh being 580-820px+, nowhere near binding), max-width is the only lever that changes the bridge's rendered size on mobile. Raised from 97% (this slot's own prior-phase value) to 99% — the tightest ceiling that still leaves a hairline safety margin against edge-to-edge touching/rounding, since the source canvas itself already has only ~1.1%/3.1% left/right margin so nothing is clipped at any percentage up to 100%. This is a real but modest further gain (~2.06% relative size increase over the already-raised 97% baseline, ~5.3% relative over the original pre-Phase-1B 94% default) — flagged honestly per instruction: the large jump already happened in the prior phase's 94%->97% change, and 97%->99% is inherently a small increment because it's this close to the format's own ceiling. Any materially bigger 'dominance' improvement would require accepting the 3:1 landscape-in-portrait-stage tension as a fixed characteristic of this specific asset, not a fixable CSS bug. max_height left at 88vh unchanged (confirmed still never binding at 99% either). PHASE 2.1 (2026-08-30, web polish pass): max_width raised 99% -> 100% and a static optical-centring correction added in css/style.css (.museum__bridge { transform: translateX(1.01%) }). Independent re-decode of the raw alpha channel at thresholds 16/32/64/128 (stable across all four) gives the visible geometry at x=17..1488 / y=162..371 of the 1536x512 canvas: bbox_w=95.77%, bbox_h=40.82%, horizontal centre at 48.99% (i.e. 1.009% LEFT of canvas centre), vertical centre at 52.05%. Because the canvas is flex-centred, that 1.009% asymmetry meant the BRIDGE ITSELF rendered off-centre: at a 375px stage its visible margins were 6.0px left vs 13.5px right. translateX(1.01%) equalises them. With the offset corrected, max_width 100% yields symmetric visible margins of 2.12% of stage width (7.9px @375, 8.3px @390/393, 9.1px @430) versus 2.59% at 99% — a ~1% linear size gain with BETTER, symmetric, still clearly intentional margins. Stated honestly: the absolute geometric ceiling is max_width 104.4% (visible content exactly edge-to-edge, zero margin), so 100% is ~96% of the theoretical maximum and no further meaningful size is available from this lever. max_height 88vh still never binding (canvas height at 100% = stage_width/3). Source PNG untouched. The remaining perceived empty space on portrait phones is inherent to a ~7:1 visible band in a portrait stage and was addressed presentationally instead (21vh caption reserve for .museum__primary = optical centring in the space actually available, plus a deliberate spatial overlap between the complete bridge and the emerging exploded structure during chapter 02 OPENING).

That is a deliberate content decision, not an automatic consequence to be taken lightly; if a loop is ever approved here it must respect the geometric-integrity rule (the bridge is never warped or split). If this slot resolves, layerFor() returns loopLayers['opening'].el instead (a genuinely separate video element per the loop_slot_contract's discovery step), breaking that identity chain: (a) the video's opacity would never be driven to 1 anywhere in the authored timeline (nothing tweens chapterEls[1] opacity during the 'opening' branch, and the later 'exploded' branch's tw(prevLayer,...) would run a 0-to-0 opacity no-op), so the video would stay invisible; and (b) primaryOuter itself would then never receive an exit tween either (its own identity would stop being chapterEls[1], and nothing else fades it), most likely leaving the still bridge_alpha PNG permanently visible underneath every later chapter. This is a choreography-authoring change in museum2d-scroll.js (out of this task's declared 'small CSS/JS guard' scope, and that file's animation logic was not to be touched), not a CSS sizing bug, so it is NOT fixed by the same primary_layer box-model correction applied to the video_transition system in this task. The primary_layer CSS/DOM-attachment fix delivered in PHASE 2.3A (see museum25d.js/style.css) DOES already fully apply to and fix the unrelated, unambiguously-scoped overview_transition_assembly/disassembly pair (chapter_key 'complete'), which is a fully independent overlay system (opacity toggled directly, not part of chapterEls/the master timeline) and has no such identity dependency.

slots.notes: PHASE 2.3 — one-shot directional transition clip, NOT an ambient loop. Copied from 03_ASSETS/Steinerne_Bruecke/2d/LOOPS/OVERVIEW/bridge_assembly_01.mp4 (existence + byte-size verified after copy). JUDGMENT CALL, stated honestly: the source folder is named OVERVIEW, but the manifest's chapter_key for this pair is 'complete', not 'overview'. Reasoning: (1) the OPENING chapter (the other primary-layer, chapter-2 slot) already has its own dedicated, still-PENDING reservation ('bridge_opening_loop', chapter_key 'opening') — reusing it for a structurally different assembly/disassembly-pair schema would collide with that existing reservation; (2) the CHAPTER_SCRIPT's only OTHER primary-layer chapter is 'complete' (chapter 10), which currently has NO video_loop/video_transition slot of any kind reserved anywhere in this manifest; (3) the brief's own worked example — 'complete→exploded uses disassembly; exploded→complete uses assembly' — describes exactly the COMPLETE chapter's behaviour: arriving at COMPLETE (from REASSEMBLY, the whole bridge re-forming) plays assembly, and leaving COMPLETE backward toward REASSEMBLY/EXPLODED plays disassembly. This pair is therefore attached to chapter_key 'complete', reusing the existing 'bridge_alpha' fallback (which the 'complete' chapter's still layer already uses via layerFor's shared primary-layer resolution) as its settle target. Because layerFor() resolves ALL three primary-layer chapters (overview/opening/complete) to the SAME physical #museumPrimary/#museumPrimaryInner container, this pair's <video> is inserted (render_target 'primary_layer') as a direct child of #museumPrimary — a sibling of #museumPrimaryInner, not a child of it, per the PHASE 2.3A small-rectangle fix (see video_transition_contract's render_target field above) — stacked above #museumBridgeImg, and is only ever triggered while the CURRENT chapter is 'complete' — it never fires for chapters 'overview' or 'opening', which remain completely unaffected static-image behaviour. | PHASE 2.4 MICRO-FIX (STONE BRIDGE OVERVIEW/STRUCTURE TRANSITION, v02 promotion): file_path repointed to a NEW direction-specific derivative cut from the single combined source 03_ASSETS/Steinerne_Bruecke/2d/LOOPS/OVERVIEW/bridge_assembly_disassembly_loop_16s_v02.mp4 (16.15s, 1080x1920, h264/yuv420p/24fps, embedded AAC audio never surfaced). A video-only web derivative (bridge_assembly_disassembly_loop_16s_v02_web.mp4, -map 0:v:0 -an -c:v copy, lossless remux) was produced first, then frame-inspected (extracted + visually compared stills at 0.1s, 2s, 4s, 6-10s in 0.125s steps, 12s, 16s, plus a frame-diff curve) to confirm it is a genuine symmetric ping-pong: COMPLETE (0s) -> EXPLODED (~8s, confirmed by a local minimum in the frame-to-frame difference curve at t=7.875-8.0s, the slowest/most settled point) -> COMPLETE (16.08s, frame diff vs t=0.1s = 0.17, i.e. a clean loop). ffprobe/showinfo confirmed an encoded I-frame at exactly pts_time=8.0s (24fps, frame 192 of 386 total), so the split at that exact frame is a lossless, frame-accurate stream copy with zero re-encode: frames 0-191 (192 frames, 8.00s) -> bridge_overview_disassembly_v02_web.mp4 (COMPLETE->EXPLODED), frames 192-385 (194 frames, 8.08s) -> bridge_overview_assembly_v02_web.mp4 (EXPLODED->COMPLETE). Boundary continuity verified by comparing the last frame of the disassembly cut against the first frame of the assembly cut (identical exploded-parts layout, no visible jump) and the first frame of the disassembly cut against the last frame of the assembly cut (both the same fully assembled bridge). Both new files copied byte-identical into the web-copy assets folder. The v01 pair (bridge_assembly_01.mp4 / bridge_disassembly_01.mp4) is preserved untouched on disk in both 03_ASSETS/.../LOOPS/OVERVIEW/ and the web-copy folder and is now LEGACY_REFERENCE_ONLY for this slot family only (see top-level 'legacy_assets' annotation) — not deleted, not overwritten.
